pageCache.pageTitle: St Thomas a Becket RC Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
"Let all that you do be done in love." - 1 Corinthians, 16:14
Welcome to St Thomas a Becket RC Primary School
As a Roman Catholic School, we value the uniqueness that God's love has created in each of us. Our core Gospel Values of service, love, faith and courage are at the centre of every part of our school life. Our school curriculum echoes these values as, each day, we try to follow God’s lead, with courage to be the best that we can be. As a school community, together with parents, carers, families and the church, we encourage each individual to develop their God given talents and skills to discover their unique potential.
Vision
& Values
Democracy Democracy is an important value at our school. Pupils have the opportunity to have their voices heard through the School Council.
Rule of law The importance of laws and rules, whether they are those that govern the class, the school or the country, are consistently reinforced throughout regular school days.
Individual liberty As a school we actively encourage pupils to make their own choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment.
Mutual Respect Our school ethos and behaviour policy centres on core Christian values such as ‘respect’ and ‘responsibility’.
Tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs This is achieved through enhancing pupil’s understanding of their place in a culturally diverse society.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Thomas a Becket RC Primary School - Welcome from our Headteacher
pageCache.text:
Welcome from our Headteacher
At St Thomas a Becket RC Primary School, our Catholic faith is at the heart of everything we do. Inspired by the Gospel values of faith, love, service and courage, we celebrate the unique gifts of every child and encourage them to become the very best version of themselves.
We are a warm, inclusive community where every child is valued, respected and nurtured. Rooted in the teachings of the Catholic Church, we welcome families from all faith backgrounds and none who wish their children to learn and grow in a caring Christian environment.
Educating the Whole Child
Our aim is to educate the whole child, supporting their academic, spiritual, social, emotional and physical development. We provide a safe and happy environment where children are challenged to achieve their potential, develop confidence and resilience, and grow into compassionate, responsible members of society.
Through a broad and enriching curriculum, we encourage every child to flourish academically, socially and spiritually, recognising and celebrating their uniqueness as a child of God.
Working in partnership with families, our parish and the wider community, we help children discover their talents, deepen their understanding of the world and develop a sense of purpose, service and respect for others.
As part of the Parish of St David's, Abbey Wood, we enjoy strong links with our parish community and work closely with families to support children in their faith journey and personal development. Together, we strive to create a community where every child feels a true sense of belonging, achievement and hope for the future.
A Happy and Thriving School
St Thomas a Becket is a happy and thriving school where children flourish, friendships grow and faith inspires hope. We are committed to ensuring that every child receives the support, encouragement and opportunities they need to succeed and enjoy their school years.
Whether you are joining us for the first time or have been part of our community for many years, you will always find a warm welcome at St Thomas a Becket. We look forward to getting to know your family, celebrating your child's successes, and working together to help them grow in faith, confidence and happiness.
Thank you for entrusting us with this important journey. We look forward to welcoming you to our St Thomas a Becket school family.
Mrs CooperHeadteacher

pageCache.text:
British Values
At St Thomas a Becket Roman Catholic School, we uphold and teach pupils about British Values, which are defined as:
Mutual Respect and Tolerance of Those with Different Faiths and Beliefs
These values are taught explicitly through Personal, Social, Health and Emotional (PSHE) and through our Religious Education. We also teach British Values through planning and delivering a broad and balanced curriculum.
The school takes opportunities to actively promote British Values through daily collective worship and whole school systems and structures such as electing and running a successful School Council.
We also actively promote British Values through ensuring that our curriculum planning and delivery includes real opportunities for exploring these values.

Wraparound Care
Breakfast & After School Club
At St Thomas a Becket, we are pleased to offer full wraparound care from 7:30am until 6:00pm, Monday to Friday, through our Becketeers’ Base Breakfast and After School Club.
We understand how important flexible childcare is for our families. Becketeers’ Base provides a safe, welcoming and enjoyable environment where children can relax, play and enjoy a range of activities with their friends before and after the school day.
Breakfast ClubOur Breakfast Club is open Monday to Friday from 7:30am until the start of the school day. Children can enjoy a selection of breakfast foods before taking part in activities and getting ready for the school day ahead.
After School Club:Our After School Club runs Monday to Friday from the end of the school day until 6:00pm. Children can enjoy a range of activities and games, spend time with their friends and relax after their school day.
Booking a Place:Sessions at Becketeers’ Base are booked and paid for through ParentMail.Before your child attends Becketeers’ Base for the first time, parents and carers must complete a New Starter Form and read and agree to our Terms & Conditions.
For further details about how Becketeers’ Base operates, please read our Club Information Booklet below.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Thomas a Becket RC Primary School - PE & Sports Premium Grant
pageCache.text:
PE & Sports Premium Grant
download_for_offlineSPORTS PREMIUM 2026
At our school, we believe that every child should have the opportunity to lead a healthy, active lifestyle and experience the enjoyment, achievement and personal growth that sport and physical activity can bring. Guided by our mission and our Gospel values of Love, Faith and Courage, we are committed to ensuring that all pupils can participate fully in high-quality physical education, competitive sport and active play, regardless of their starting point, ability or background.
The Primary PE and Sport Premium provides funding to improve the quality of PE, sport and physical activity across the school. We use this funding strategically to enhance teaching and learning, increase participation, develop staff expertise and provide a wide range of sporting opportunities that inspire children to be active for life.
All children receive two PE lessons each week, developing their physical literacy, fitness, confidence and teamwork skills. In EYFS and Year 1, children benefit from high-quality Continuous Provision opportunities that support the development of gross motor skills through active and engaging play. Our Forest School programme further enriches physical development through outdoor learning experiences that build resilience, coordination and confidence.
We are committed to inclusion and ensuring that every child can access physical activity. All Key Stage 2 pupils participate in swimming lessons, including children with SEND. Additional support is provided for pupils with the most complex needs to ensure full participation and success.
Children have access to a wide range of extracurricular and enrichment opportunities throughout the year, including lunchtime clubs, football, dodgeball and active wraparound care activities. Our annual Sports Day and participation in the Mini Marathon encourage all pupils to challenge themselves, demonstrate perseverance and celebrate achievement.
We are proud to provide opportunities for children to represent the school in local and borough competitions, including cricket, indoor athletics, Sportshall Championships, basketball, dodgeball and football. Year 5 and Year 6 pupils also participate in local girls' and boys' football leagues, developing sportsmanship, teamwork and competitive experience.
Further opportunities are provided through cricket coaching for Key Stage 2 pupils and our partnership with Charlton Athletic, including participation in programmes such as The Joy of Moving, which promote physical wellbeing, positive mental health and healthy lifestyles.
Through the effective use of our PE and Sport Premium funding, we aim to:
Through our values of Love, Faith and Courage, we inspire children to be active, resilient and confident learners. Through a high-quality PE curriculum and a wide range of enrichment opportunities, we promote lifelong participation in physical activity and sport, ensuring that every pupil, regardless of ability or need, can develop their physical literacy, wellbeing, confidence and enjoyment of being active. Our PE and Sport Premium funding plays a key role in providing inclusive opportunities that enable all children to participate, achieve and flourish.
Guided by our values of Love, Faith and Courage, we are committed to helping every child discover the joy of physical activity and sport. Through high-quality teaching, inclusive provision and a rich programme of sporting opportunities, we nurture healthy, confident and resilient children who are equipped with the skills, motivation and enthusiasm to lead active lives both now and in the future.
Develop children's physical literacy, confidence and wellbeing.

A Guide For Parents
A Guide For Parents
Relationships & Health Education (RHE) 2026–2027
At St Thomas a Becket, our teaching about relationships, health and growing up is rooted in our Catholic faith and in the belief that every person is created, chosen and loved by God.
What is Life to the Full?
Life to the Full is Ten Ten Resources’ Relationships and Health Education programme for Catholic primary schools. It provides age-appropriate lessons from EYFS to Year 6 and helps children learn about relationships, physical and emotional health, personal safety, growing and changing, life online and living well with others. The programme uses stories, discussion, activities, video, prayer and reflection.
The programme is taught as a spiral curriculum: important ideas are revisited as children grow, with teaching becoming more detailed and developmentally appropriate over time.
The three Life to the Full modules
Created and Loved by God
Children learn about their unique dignity, their bodies, health, emotions, growing and changing, and how to make healthy choices.
Created to Love Others
Children learn about family, friendship, kindness, respectful relationships, boundaries, online relationships and how to keep themselves and others safe.
Created to Live in Community
Children learn that they belong to wider communities and are called to love and serve others, contribute to the Common Good and live responsibly in the world.
What will my child learn?
Across the programme, children learn about themes including:
Teaching is adapted to the age, stage and needs of the children. Where appropriate, staff also adapt resources and approaches so that pupils with SEND can access the learning successfully.
their uniqueness, dignity and value
healthy friendships and family relationships
feelings, emotional wellbeing and resilience
physical health, hygiene and healthy choices
safe and respectful behaviour, including online
responsibility, service, community and the Common Good
What is statutory?
Relationships Education and Health Education are statutory in primary schools in England. Parents do not have a right to withdraw their child from these areas. Primary schools may also teach additional sex education beyond the statutory Science curriculum; where this is taught, parents are informed and the school’s policy explains the right to request withdrawal from that additional content.
Our approach at St Thomas a Becket
We want children to receive clear, age-appropriate teaching that helps them to be safe, healthy, respectful and confident, while reflecting the teachings and values of the Catholic Church. Our partnership with parents is an important part of this work.
